entertainment.title: Dax Shepard Reacts to Claims His, Kristen Bell's Marriage Is "Abusive"
entertainment.summary: Dax Shepard is setting the record straight. Two weeks after Kristen Bell shared that her husband flirts with her by complimenting their waiter or waitress while on a date, the Parenthood actor...
entertainment.body:
Two weeks after Kristen Bell shared that her husband flirts with her by complimenting their waiter or waitress while on a date, the Parenthood actor addressed misconceptions about their 13-year-old marriage.

"Another round of me being a terrible person was in the media, and I avoided that," Shepard began on the Nov. 9 episode of his Armchair Expert podcast. "But then it hit Kristen's doorstep really hard, and then I got to find out everything that people are saying about me."

He argued that there is "a level of unjustness" regarding the perception of his behavior, noting that there is "this weird narrative that is surrounding me as controlling, abusive, now flirting with people in public, which I don't do."

The 51-year-old acknowledged that the way Bell—with whom he shares two daughters—explained their dynamic on the Oct. 26 episode of his podcast alongside her Nobody Wants This costars could have been misconstrued.

"I think she phrased it in a way that got intentionally, easily confused for people because we're saying I flirt with Kristen by tipping people a lot and I flirt with Kristen by complimenting people," Shepard said, "If you think I'm complimenting hot young waitresses, you got a problem."

"I'm finding the dude that I don't think has had a compliment in a while and tell him I love his shoes," he clarified. "It's always somebody that I want to make their day. So those compliments are flirting with Kristen. But it got to be, when it went through the grinder, that I flirt with people in front of Kristen."

The podcast host also shut down speculations that he abuses his wife or their kids.

"For me, growing up around certain men who behaved a certain way, and then literally dedicating my whole life to being the opposite of all that," he shared, "I don't ever yell at my children. I don't swear at them. I don't yell at my wife. To have given it my all to be the opposite of what, now, some group of people is saying I am is hard."

Russell Brand’s wife, Laura Gallacher, has been “totally brainwashed” by him, her family claims.

Gallacher has stood by the disgraced British comedian’s side, even as he was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison Monday following his conviction on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault .

“Russell gets what Russell wants. He has that charm and swagger, and Laura is besotted with him,” a source told the outlet. “She goes along with what he wants, it’s like he has totally brainwashed her.”

The source said they are hopeful that with Brand behind bars, Gallacher might be able to get away from the alleged hold he has on her.

“This is her chance, if she wishes to take it, to start her life with someone far, far nicer than Russell,” the source said.

One family friend said Gallacher has been in shock since Brand was handed his verdict Thursday. While he was convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault, he was found not guilty of two other rape charges and a count of attempted indecent assault.

The “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” star had pleaded not guilty to all charges and denied all allegations .

entertainment.title: Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama ‘I Is Another’ Sells Wide Ahead of AFM
entertainment.summary: The Felix Randau-directed historical film about Heinrich Himmler’s massage therapist premiered to strong reviews at Locarno.
entertainment.body:
Beta Cinema has closed a raft of international sales for I Is Another , Felix Randau’s historical drama starring Claes Bang and Valerie Pachner, ahead of the American Film Market.

ARP Selection acquired all rights for France, with further deals signed with Youplanet Pictures for Spain, Angel Films for Scandinavia, Big Tree Entertainment for India and Palace Films for Australia and New Zealand. Vertigo Media took Hungary, Beta Film acquired Bulgaria and Red Cape picked up Israel.

The deals were unveiled Monday on the eve of AFM , following the film’s world premiere on Locarno’s Piazza Grande this summer. Related Stories Business The Hollywood Reporter Launches Turkish Edition Movies Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy to Star in Oliver Sacks Love Story 'Insomniac City'

Based on true events, I Is Another stars Bang as Felix Kersten, massage therapist to SS leader Heinrich Himmler . Said to have helped secure the release of thousands of concentration camp prisoners, Kersten is traveling to Oslo in the hope of winning the Nobel Peace Prize. Aboard the night train, however, he faces an interview with Hedda (Pachner), a journalist convinced he is an impostor. Their encounter becomes a contest over memory, truth and the version of his life Kersten wants the world to believe.

Port-au-Prince Pictures will release the film in Germany in early 2027. ARP Selection is introducing it to French audiences at the Augenblick Film Festival ahead of a nationwide theatrical release next year.

Randau ( Iceman , Northern Star ) wrote and directed the film, which was produced by Ostlicht Filmproduktion in co-production with Veit Heiduschka’s Wega Film. The cast also includes Susanne Wuest, Timocin Ziegler and Martin Müller, with Sebastian Thaler serving as director of photography.

Beta Cinema will hold an AFM screening on Nov. 11 at 9 a.m. at AMC Century City 3. The American Film Market runs Nov. 10-15.

entertainment.body:
Sarah Paulson made an unusual request of her “All’s Fair” castmate, Glenn Close . Cynthia Nixon is pleased that her mild-mannered “Gilded Age” character is developing a backbone. “It’s really nice to see her finally growing into herself and believing that she has the power to say no,” the actress told PageSix.com’s Nicki Gostin at the HBO show’s splashy Season 4 premiere. “You know, Jane Fonda said this wonderful thing. She said, ‘No is a full sentence,’ and it took me a lot of years to learn that.” The “Sex and the City” alum, 60, admitted that she’s “still learning” that lesson. After the screening, Nixon, along with the rest of the cast, partied at the Plaza Hotel, which will close in January for a four-year restoration project.

It doesn’t penetrate me anymore. I have put out so much history and facts about the Jewish people, the Jewish history, and there is a thing called Google; you can go and get the answers.” The “Will & Grace” alum added that she “never imagined in a million years that our generation would be facing such a resurgence of such an ancient hate.” Messing said that a silver lining has been “the people that I’ve met in the Jewish community. I have made so many new friends. It has been really nourishing for me.”

entertainment.summary: Dominic Cooke will direct the adaptation of Bill Hayes’ memoir, with Altitude launching worldwide sales at AFM.
entertainment.body:
Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy are set to star in Insomniac City , director Dominic Cooke’s adaptation of writer and photographer Bill Hayes’ memoir about his romance with celebrated neurologist Oliver Sacks.

The casting was unveiled Monday on the eve of the American Film Market in Los Angeles, where Altitude will introduce the project to international buyers.

Bailey ( Bridgerton ) will play Hayes opposite Nighy ( About Time ) as Sacks. Adapted from Hayes’ 2017 memoir, the film follows his move from San Francisco to New York in the aftermath of a devastating loss. As he rebuilds his life, Hayes unexpectedly falls in love with both his adopted city and Sacks, beginning a relationship that transformed both men’s lives during the neurologist’s final years. Sacks’ work famously includes The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat and Awakenings , the latter adapted into the Oscar-nominated film starring Robin Williams and Robert De Niro.

Cooke, whose directing credits include The Courier and On Chesil Beach , co-wrote the screenplay with Hayes.

“ Insomniac City is a rare story that feels both profoundly intimate and epic in scope,” Cooke said in a statement. “It is also a love letter to New York City itself, a place of endless possibility, reinvention and connection.”

entertainment.title: Ye & Ty Dolla $ign Stole ‘Vultures 1’ Sample From Longtime Friend, Lawsuit Claims
entertainment.summary: The case, the latest of many against Kanye, claims the two stars never paid for a sample that appeared in their "Vultures" collab.
entertainment.body:
A new lawsuit claims Ye (formerly Ye ) and Ty Dolla $ign stole a sample featured in their 2023 song “Vultures” — and moreover, that they ripped it off from one of Ty’s longtime friends after overhearing it on a phone call.

The case, the latest in a long list of such accusations against Ye, was filed by producers Jaraed Deal and Marlon Barrow over the hit song, which was the lead single off the controversial rapper’s chart-topping Vultures 1 and reached No. 38 on the Hot 100.

The lawsuit accuses Ye and Ty (Tyrone William Griffin, Jr.) of unilaterally taking a sample from a 2018 track Deal and Barrow had co-created to shop to recording artists, a move they say shows a “blatant disregard for their artistic contributions and legal rights.”

“This action is not only about unpaid licensing fees and the lack of appropriate credit, but also about the essential right of any artist to determine when, how, and by whom their creative work is used,” lawyers for the pair write in the lawsuit, obtained and first reported by Billboard .

Such accusers often face difficulty proving a star had access to a song in order to steal it; many lawsuits are dismissed on the grounds that an artist likely never even heard the original. But Deal and Barrow say that won’t be a problem for the new case over “Vultures.”

Their lawyers allege Barrow has had a “close personal and professional relationship” with Ty “spanning decades,” and that the star directly asked for a copy of the song after he “heard the sampled works playing in the background” during a phone call.

Barrow says he sent the track to Ty assuming that a full written licensing deal would be signed if it was ever used. Such an agreement was allegedly never reached, but the lawsuit says the sample was used on “Vultures” anyway. Barrow is credited on the song as a producer, but the lawsuit says neither Deal nor Barrow ever consented to the sample or were paid for it.

“This action concerns the knowing, continuous, and blatant unauthorized use of the sampled works,” their attorneys write. “It concerns protecting artistic integrity, enforcing intellectual property rights, and preventing commercial exploitation.”

entertainment.title: Caitlin Clark Wrote a Rhyming Book With a Positive Message to Kids About Being a Little Extra
entertainment.summary: EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams is the WNBA star's debut children's book and has already become a Number One bestseller
entertainment.body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams marks Caitlin Clark ’s first children’s book. The basketball player wrote the rhyming picture book herself, with illustrations by Romanian artist Adriana Predoi. Published Nov. 3, her debut has already climbed to the Number One bestseller spot on Amazon and is aimed at readers ages four to eight. The book turns a message rooted in Clark’s own childhood into an upbeat story for young readers.

The sentiment behind EXTRAordinary relates to a mirror in Clark’s childhood bedroom. As the Indiana Fever guard told NBC’s Today on the day of its release, before she was born, her parents had a mirror made with the words, “The difference between ordinary and extraordinary is the little EXTRA.” That message became a personal reminder to put extra effort into pursuing her dreams and career as a pro basketball player.

Clark also noted how far women’s sports have come, pointing to new WNBA teams, nationally televised coverage of women’s sports , and a growing inventory of WNBA signature sneakers . “We’re just scratching the surface,” said Clark.

EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams gives readers a closer look at the values Clark credits with helping her succeed beyond basketball. Rather than focusing solely on athletic achievements, the book celebrates the importance of family, friendships, and teammates. And its rhyming format and colorful illustrations make the message accessible to younger children. The central takeaway is that pursuing big ambitions matters, but so does appreciating the people who help make those dreams possible.

The book cover also features a few Easter eggs on the jerseys for fans to discover. Each jersey number has a connection to Clark’s life, representing her familiar basketball number (22), her father’s college jersey number (6), the number she wore during high school (11), and her Team USA tryout number (17).

Although EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams is Clark’s debut as a children’s author; this isn’t the first children’s book about Clark.

Fans of the WNBA player who want a chronological account of her life and rise to fame may also consider Caitlin Clark: A Little Golden Book Biography , written by Marisa DiNovis and illustrated by Joanie Stone.

As Variety reports, Gunn and his co-CEO and chairman, Peter Safran, will both leave their posts at DC Studios. They will be replaced by Jeremy Latcham, who spent years working at rival Marvel Studios before starting his own production company in 2017.

In a statement shared on Instagram, Gunn recalled his childhood in Manchester, Missouri, where he would draw his own comics “with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters.” He continued, “Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn’t know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn’t pass up the unique opportunity. I’m glad I took the job.”

Gunn and Safran were tapped to lead DC Studios in 2022. At the time, DC — despite having the likes of Superman, Batman, Aquaman, and the Green Lantern in their IP locker — was struggling to keep pace with Marvel, which was one of the most dominant forces in Hollywood. Gunn was a big part of Marvel’s success, too, thanks to his helming of the Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy.

During their tenure at DC, Gunn and Safran enjoyed some success, most prominently with Gunn’s own Superman , which garnered strong reviews and a $618 million global box office. This year, the horror flick Clayface enjoyed solid box office success on a small budget, though the Superman spin-off, Supergirl was unable to make back its $170 million budget. (It’s worth noting, too, that some of these struggles may not have been DC Studios specific, as superhero movies in general have become less of a box office certainty since their late 2010s/early 2020s peak.)

entertainment.title: The Beach Boys Cancel Final Remaining 2026 Concert Date
entertainment.summary: Troubled run was supposed to wrap in Bristol, Virginia, but was cancelled like many before it
entertainment.body:
The Beach Boys have cancelled the vast majority of their concerts over the past three months as Mike Love battles a severe health ailment that he’s not yet made public, and by this week, the final remaining show on their 2026 itinerary was a November 13 stop at the Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Bristol, Virginia. But according to Ticketmaster, they’ve just cancelled that one as well, meaning the only remaining concert on their public calendar is a makeup date at the River Cree Resort and Casino in Alberta, Canada, on May 8, 2027.

A new group billing itself as John Stamos and the California Sound were swapped in for the Beach Boys at Disney World’s Epcot Center on November 11 and 12. But the November 13 show at the Hard Rock Hotel & Casino was simply cancelled. (All acts at Epcot Center play three truncated shows in a single evening. That means the Beach Boys were essentially planning on playing seven concerts in three days.)

Throughout late 2025, Beach Boys fans expressed increasing alarm with Love’s increasingly gaunt appearance and raspy singing voice. In February, veteran Beach Boys band member Bruce Johnston, who joined the group in 1965, left the touring band. “I am excited to join the Beach Boys for performances on special occasions and will see everyone at the Hollywood Bowl as we celebrate our nation’s 250th birthday!” he told fans. “This isn’t goodbye, it’s see you soon. I am forever grateful to be a part of the Beach Boys musical legacy.”

But Johnston didn’t make an appearance at the Hollywood Bowl. And by the time the tour reached that famous L.A. venue in early July, Love’s appearance was even more alarming. Weeks later, the group pulled 30 concerts. “We’ve been having a blast out there, and to keep the good vibrations going strong, we’ll be taking a short break to recharge before getting back on the road in September,” Love wrote to fans. “Thanks for your love — we can’t wait to see you back out there for a September to Remember.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

When September came around, the Beach Boys cancelled even more shows. They finally emerged October 3 for a private event at the Waldorf Astoria Monarch Beach in Dana Point, California. Photos and brief videos that emerged showed Love performing from a chair. And a week later, they played a pair of shows in Cincinnati and Nashville where Love remained seated all night, barely singing.

entertainment.title: R&B and disco legend Rochelle Fleming dead at 72
entertainment.summary: The First Choice lead singer died on Nov. 5.
entertainment.body:
First Choice lead singer Rochelle Fleming has died . She was 72.

The R&B and disco legend passed away on Thursday in Philadelphia, according to a statement shared via her Instagram the following day.

“She bought light, laughter and love to the world,” the Friday announcement read.

Fleming’s longtime manager, George Iz Correia, mourned her in a social media statement , writing, “Although my heartbreak is unbearable and the gravity of the situation hit at the most sporadic times, I have so many wonderful memories with Rochelle that I can’t help but smile with immense gratitude.”

Correia praised Fleming’s kind heart, saying she “never uttered a harsh word about anyone … unless you were chewing gum.”

“She despised referring to her supporters as ‘fans.’ You were ALL known affectionately as her ‘sweeties,'” Correia stated, sharing that the “Love Itch” songstress would not want anyone “sad during this time.”

“So let’s continue to celebrate her and the legacy of ‘First Choice’s’ music,” he added, before signing off, “Sleep on Ro, I love and miss you. Love, ‘G.'”

Fleming was also mourned by Christian Hope Baptist Church, which she attended as a child and “remained a faithful member all her life.”

entertainment.title: Dr. Dre Says He’s Going ‘Off the Grid’ for the First Time in His Career: ‘I’m Going to Go Away’
entertainment.summary: "What if there’s something else waiting for me that could give me the same exact feeling when I discovered music?" he pondered.
entertainment.body:
Dr. Dre is finally taking a break. The legendary producer synonymous with West Coast rap music has essentially been in the studio either physically or mentally every day since he started his career with the World Class Wrecking Crew in 1984. But he sat down with Ice Cube and Mike Epps for their new podcast Listen and Laugh , and revealed that he may be taking a break from making music for the first time in a long time.

“For the first time in my entire adult career, I’m going to take a break from that,” he said on the Nov. 6 episode when talking about his work process. “I’m going to go away, and I’m going to get off the grid for a year or two and come back.”

Adding that he was always thinking about making music even when he wasn’t in the studio. “You never leave it,” he continued. “Even when you’re outside of the studio, you’re looking at storefronts or bumper stickers or some s–t like that, that could give you an idea for the next time that you go in the studio. So, you’re never away from it. You’re always tethered to this thing and for the first time in my life, I won’t be. What if there’s something else waiting for me that could give me the same exact feeling when I discovered music?”

Elsewhere in the interview, he double down on his stance on AI.

“I’m extremely excited about AI,” he said. “I love it. I love the potential of it. I love the idea of where it could possibly go, you know, with music, with film. Like, what happens if someone says, ‘I’m going to pay you to be in my movie.’ Right. You don’t even have to be there, but you get to approve what they do. It’s your image and your voice. What’s wrong with that? It’s just a whole new level of creativity.”

Back in August, he told The New York Times that he sees the new technology as being a “new tool for creativity.”

“I had a discussion with a few people a few days ago,” he said. “They were against AI and I’m like, ‘OK, you sound like the person that would have been against the drum machine when it came out.’ Or synthesizers, right? It’s a new tool for creativity. Some people are afraid of learning new things.”

entertainment.title: ‘The Gilded Age’ Is Serving Up Ambition and Shame in Season 4 Return
entertainment.summary: Series bosses Julian Fellowes and Sonja Warfield, along with various cast members, weigh in on the HBO gem's fourth season.
entertainment.body:
Logo text [This story contains spoilers from The Gilded Age season four premiere.]

The Gilded Age is officially back. And while that world is still turning, it’s not quite moving in the way many fans had predicted.

After a third season filled with dramatic deaths and near-deaths — not to mention an arranged marriage motivated by power and position later punished with an unexpected sacrifice of the heart and an exciting wedding proposal — season four’s first episode “Ring the Bells,” directed by executive producer Salli Richardson-Whitfield , immediately kicks off with another seesaw of emotions. Related Stories TV Chuck Lorre Talks David Ellison Optimism, Scientology and the Perks (Really!) of Working for Roseanne Barr Movies 'All That She Wants' Review: Annie Murphy Is All That in a Fizzy Rom-Com That Works Best When It Isn't Trying Too Hard

In England, Gladys — as many women, even the wealthy ones, of that era did — experiences the life-threatening birth of her first child with the loving Duke she was forced to marry, and now adores, by her side , while Oscar van Rhijn trades “I do’s” with his bride ( yes, bride! ) Enid Winterton, the new Mrs. Oscar van Rhijn.

Gilded Age creator, executive producer and writer Julian Fellowes tells The Hollywood Reporter that the first episode featured the van Rhijn wedding because “we wanted to have the fun of catching everyone out so that at the beginning they think that they’re going to be watching one of the weddings they’ve been expecting, and this is one of them they haven’t been expecting.”

Element of surprise aside, Fellowes adds that “it’s nice to have a group scene to start a series off. You want to show a lot of your characters and the world they’re operating in so that your public can become reacquainted with the whole setup. If you start a series with a two-hander of two people sitting in a sitting room talking, it doesn’t quite do the same thing. You’re saying to the viewer, ‘You’re back in our world, and here we all are.’”

This season, the show feels even more personal. “We wanted to test all of the relationships within the show. So marriages, romances, familial relationships. I think the social mobility that is inherent to America is also something that’s tested, and we get to see who gets to move up socially, where they get to go,” says Fellowes’ The Gilded Age collaborator Sonja Warfield, who serves as executive producer and writer alongside Fellowes.

entertainment.title: Tate McRae’s ‘Housewife’ No. 1 on Global Charts for Third Week, Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ on the Prowl
entertainment.summary: Jackson places a third song in the Global 200’s top 10 this year.
entertainment.body:
Tate McRae ’s “Housewife” adds a third week at No. 1 on both the Billboard Global 200 and Billboard Global Excl. U.S. , two weeks after it debuted at the summit of both surveys.

The song remains the biggest hit in the world with 48.8 million streams (down 24%) and 2,000 sold (down 38%) globally Oct. 30-Nov. 5, according to Luminate. It totaled 37.2 million streams (down 22%) outside the U.S.

Karol G, Judeline and rusowsky’s “BbY WOW” keeps at No. 2 after six weeks atop the Global 200 since September and ADÉLA’s “Nicole Kidman” is steady at No. 3, one spot off its peak.

Michael Jackson ’s “Thriller” bounds 22-4 for a new Global 200 high (surpassing its prior No. 18 best, reached a year ago this week), up 78% to 33.2 million streams and 53% to 6,000 sold worldwide in the tracking week that included Halloween. The late King of Pop posts his third top 10 on the chart, all achieved this year — “Billie Jean” led for a week and “Beat It” hit No. 5, both in May, boosted by buzz for the record-setting biopic Michael . All three songs are from Jackson’s landmark 1983 album , Thriller .

Rounding out the Global 200’s top five, Ashe’s “Stop the Wedding!” holds at its No. 5 high.

Elsewhere in the Global Excl. U.S. top five, “BbY WOW” repeats at No. 2, likewise after six weeks at No. 1 since September; “Nicole Kidman” is again No. 3, after reaching No. 2; “Stop the Wedding!” marches 7-4 for its first week in the region; and ADÉLA’s “Ain’t in LA” lifts 6-5, after hitting No. 4.

The Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. U.S. charts rank songs based on streaming and sales activity culled from more than 200 territories around the world, as compiled by Luminate. The Global 200 is inclusive of worldwide data and the Global Excl. U.S. chart comprises data from territories excluding the United States.

Chart ranks are based on a weighted formula incorporating official-only streams on both subscription and ad-supported tiers of audio and video music services, as well as download sales, the latter of which reflect purchases from full-service digital music retailers from around the world, with sales from direct-to-consumer (D2C) sites excluded from the charts’ calculations.

entertainment.title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Directors Board Animated Short ‘Living With a Visionary’ as Exec Producers (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans join Stephen P. Neary's documentary about a poet’s 50-year marriage to an art curator grappling with Parkinson’s, which is narrated by James Cromwell.
entertainment.body:
KPop Demon Hunters directors and Oscar winners Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans have boarded the award-winning animated short film Living With a Visionary as executive producers.

Narrated by James Cromwell, the documentary, written, directed and animated by Stephen P. Neary, is a reflection on a poet’s 50-year marriage to an art curator grappling with Parkinson’s. The news comes before The New York Times Op-Docs will premiere the short this week.

Living With a Visionary recently won the grand jury award for animation at AFI Fest after earlier this year being honored with the short film jury award for animation at the Sundance Film Festival. Related Stories Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Shame and Money' Director Explains Why His Int'l Oscar Hopeful About Dignity Feels So Physical Music Carly Rae Jepsen Set to Host 2027 Juno Awards

The film, an adaptation of John Matthias’ memoir of the same name, explores the “bittersweet reflection on John’s relationship with his beloved wife Diana, and how it is transformed by the effects of her Parkinson’s treatment,” reads a synopsis. “As Diana’s medication besets her with vivid, often beautiful hallucinations, John, now her caregiver, adapts to her imaginary world.”

Produced by Neary and Mireia Vilanova, the film consists of thousands of drawings, illustrated by hand on intersecting layers of vellum. The creator drew them over the course of three years at nights and on weekends while working full-time as a story artist and teaching classes at the California Institute of the Arts.

Neary is known as the creator and showrunner of The Fungies! on Cartoon Network and HBO Max and the supervising producer on the Annie-nominated show Clarence . As a story artist, his credits include KPop Demon Hunters , The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs , Rio and The Peanuts Movie .

“Somehow while working full-time on KPop Demon Hunters and raising a family, Stephen found the time to make this heartbreaking, beautiful film,” said Kang. “I don’t know how he did it, and honestly I’m worried he doesn’t sleep enough, but we’re so excited for more audiences to see Living With a Visionary. The world needs unique stories in animation and often the most impactful ones come from the least expected places.”

Appelhans shared: “Stephen’s film feels like a sketch of the human soul. This assembly of lines that somehow captures love, grief, hallucination and connection. I got to live inside Cromwell’s narration and experience the heartache of being alive alongside the enduring power of love. A truly special piece of documentary filmmaking.”

entertainment.title: James Gunn “Incredibly Relieved” to Leave DC Studios: Job Was “Trying, to Say the Least”
entertainment.summary: The DC Studios co-chief admits that the executive role wasn't quite right for him and looks forward to returning to filmmaking full time.
entertainment.body:
Logo text James Gunn wasn’t entirely happy as DC Studios co-chief anyway.

That’s according to Gunn, who posted a farewell message on Instagram in the wake of the surprising news that he and Peter Safran were exiting the top studio roles and Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham was taking over.

The Superman and Guardians of the Galaxy director expressed eagerness to return to full-time creative work rather than split his attention with managing a studio.

“What only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least,” he wrote. “I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that) … And the thing my ADHD hyperfocus has had the most difficulty with has been dividing my time between projects I’m incredibly passionate about and the ones I’m not so much and all the things I have to do as a studio head … So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I’m also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking.” Related Stories Movies DC Studios Shocker: James Gunn, Peter Safran Stepping Down with Marvel Alum Jeremy Latcham to Take Over Movies 'Clayface' Director James Watkins on the Tragic Ending, Joker Easter Eggs and His Star's Secret Injury

Gunn also had praise for some of the “high points” of the job such as releasing Superman and Clayface , and making the HBO series Peacemaker — though notably didn’t mention the box office disappointment Supergirl .

“That’s not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes,” Gunn added. “We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we’ve just been engaged on another DC project which I’m writing, and we’ll see where it goes after that.”

The exit news came in the wake of Skydance completing its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery last month and despite Gunn being apparently reassured that he would continue at the studio. Latcham has credits on many MCU titles (including Gunn’s first Guardians ) and has been considered Marvel head Kevin Feige’s right-hand man.

Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios.

entertainment.title: Ridley Scott Will Miss Academy’s Governors Awards, Accept Honorary Oscar Remotely (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The 88-year-old, who is based in London, underwent a minor medical procedure last week and has been advised not to fly while he is still healing, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter.
entertainment.body:
The legendary filmmaker Ridley Scott , who was tapped to receive an honorary Oscar at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’ 17th annual Governors Awards on Sunday night, will not be able to attend the ceremony in Hollywood to accept the honor in-person, The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report.

Scott, who is based in London and will turn 89 on Nov. 30, underwent a minor medical procedure last week and has been advised not to fly while he is still healing, sources tell THR . However, Scott’s entire family — his wife, children and grandchildren — will be making the trip to L.A. for this celebration. Related Stories Movies 'You Can See Everything' Sweeps Critics Choice Documentary Awards TV George R.R. Martin Tapped for Lifetime Achievement Nod at Infinity Festival (Exclusive)

Scott pre-taped his acceptance speech last week, and it will be played during the ceremony, at which actress Glenn Close and animator Floyd Norman will also receive honorary Oscars and producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler will be presented with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award.

Scott has had a career unlike any other. He was nearly 40 when he made his directorial debut with 1977’s The Duellists , having spent his early career making high-end commercials in partnership with his brother Tony. But he has made up — and continues to make up — for lost time, consistently pumping out action-packed blockbusters (his films have collectively grossed some $5 billion), many of them landmarks of cinematic achievement. Indeed, he is behind two of the most significant sci-fi films of all time, 1979’s Alien and 1982’s Blade Runner , as well as 1991’s Thelma & Louise (for which he received a best director Oscar nomination), 2000’s Gladiator (which won the best picture Oscar, while he lost best director), 2001’s Black Hawk Down (for which he received his most recent best director Oscar nom), 2007’s American Gangster , 2015’s The Martian and 2024’s Gladiator 2 .

He has also produced many of his films — among them Thelma & Louise , Black Hawk Down , American Gangster , The Martian (for which he personally received a best picture Oscar nom) and Gladiator 2 — as well as a ton of TV series including The Good Wife , The Man in the High Castle , The Good Fight and Dope Thief .

Though he projects the image of the most masculine of males, and has featured tough-guy characters in films like Blade Runner and Gladiator , he is also behind truly feminist films like Alien and Thelma & Louise . His works collectively have been nominated for 45 Oscars (including seven for performances), winning nine (including one for a performance), but he has never taken home a statuette.

entertainment.title: Robbie Williams Defends Olivia Rodrigo Against Plagiarism Claims
entertainment.summary: No, Robbie Williams doesn't think that Olivia Rodrigo is a traitor. The "Angels" singer responded to accusations online that Rodrigo's new holiday song "Take Me Home (4 Christmas)" ripped off his...
entertainment.body:
No, Robbie Williams doesn't think that Olivia Rodrigo is a traitor.

The "Angels" singer responded to accusations online that Rodrigo's new holiday song "Take Me Home (4 Christmas)" ripped off his 2012 hit "Candy," which he stressed he "couldn't care less" about.

"I love Olivia Rodrigo," Williams said in a statement posted to Instagram Nov. 9. "I've loved her since 'Brutal.' What a f--king record. I wish I'd made it. Also, I cannot believe how much she swears on stage. And that's coming from me. I'm a Sweary Mary, but she's making me look like a Victorian schoolmistress."

"It sounds to me as though she may have accidentally stumbled across a musical echo of mine in one of her new songs," he continued. "And do you know what? I couldn't care less."

"I don't want to know," he declared. "I'm not going after her. Because I think at some point, some f--king sanity has to prevail."

The Take That alum hoped to make a broader point in his resistance to taking issue with whatever perceived similarities exist between "Candy" and "Take Me Home," because "artists deserve to be protected."

"There's a difference between protecting your work and treating every vaguely familiar sequence of notes as a winning lottery ticket," Williams explained. "Some of this stuff has become ambulance chasing. And I think it's disgusting."

"We all stand on the shoulders of people who came before us," he added. "Somethings consciously. Sometimes without even knowing it. That's how music works. If we keep punishing people for accidentally arriving somewhere somebody else has already been, eventually we're going to frighten the creativity out of everyone."

entertainment.summary: The rocker also reveals what fans can expect from his next album.
entertainment.body:
On Nov. 14, Billy Idol will be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s class of 2026 in Los Angeles, along with his longtime co-writer, guitarist and friend Steven Stevens.

The timing is especially meaningful for Idol: 2026 marks 50 years since the British rocker started making music in punk band Generation X in 1976. He later went solo and became a global superstar with blistering, sneering Hot 100 hits such as “White Wedding,” “Rebel Yell” and “Cradle of Love.”

Ahead of the induction ceremony, the City of Los Angeles has declared Nov. 13 Billy Idol Day; to mark the occasion, Idol and Stevens will play a free acoustic show at the very un-rocker time of 10 a.m. Performing, no matter the time, continues to be a thrill. “We’re going to do it while we can,” says Idol. “Rocking till we drop.”

Idol, 70, talked to Billboard about what the Rock Hall honor means to him and what’s next.

It’s incredibly wild. I fell in love with rock’n’roll when I was 7 years old, so I started to dream about being in a group and writing songs and making music from [then on].

Why do you think this year was your year after not getting elected last year?

I’m not sure. Maybe it’s because there’s a number of other English people going in this year: Phil Collins, New Order, Joy Division, Oasis. I know sometimes it does take a couple of years.

It’d be great to see Noel [Gallagher from Oasis]. He came and saw us in South America when we played. I did a charity [version of The Who’s] Tommy with Phil Collins in 1989. He was [Uncle Ernie], I was Cousin Kevin.

entertainment.summary: A select few hits have led the chart for at least 10 weeks — and 20-plus.
entertainment.body:
Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement.

Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.)

In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024.

On the Sept. 5, 2026-dated Hot 100, Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” became the sole longest-leading non-holiday hit, with its 20th week at No. 1. As of the Nov. 14 survey, it’s the overall record holder with 27 weeks, having surpassed Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” which has jingled to No. 1 for 22 weeks over each holiday season since December 2019.

In honor of the singles that have claimed the Hot 100’s top spot the longest, here’s a look at the elite leaders to rule for double-digit weeks.

“It feels surreal,” Langley told Billboard News earlier in 2026 of the song’s impact. “I think this has been the biggest moment for me, where I’ve seen where fans can change your career. For so long, you’re like, ‘Alright, one song at a time, one record at a time.’ But with this one song — and they’ve done it continuously for me — but really with ‘Choosin’ Texas’ … man, have they taken ahold of it. It’s wild.”

entertainment.title: Paul McCartney Is a Billionaire — and the World’s Third-Richest Musician — According to Forbes
entertainment.summary: The former Beatle made his fortune by investing in other artists' music.
entertainment.body:
Paul McCartney sang in 1964, “I don’t care too much for money — money can’t buy me love.” More than six decades later, the former Beatle is officially a billionaire, according to Forbes .

The financial publication declared Monday (Nov. 9) that McCartney’s fortune has surpassed $1.4 billion, making him the third-richest musician in the world. Only Jay-Z and Taylor Swift, whose net worths are $2.8 billion and $2 billion, respectively, are above him, Forbes estimates.

McCartney is famously savvy with his investments, having learned the hard way how to navigate finances after he and ex-bandmates Ringo Starr, John Legend and George Harrison famously earned very little within the restrictive confines of their initial record contract. The Wings frontman was eventually able to reclaim some ownership of the catalog through lawsuits and renegotiations circa 2017, but before that, he built much of his fortune by starting his publishing company, MPL Communications, and buying the rights to enduring hits that still see returns to this day.

These include Christmas standards such as “Baby, It’s Cold Outside” and “Blue Christmas,” as well as other classics including “Blue Suede Shoes” and the scores to musicals such as Grease .

Of course, the Liverpool legend is also a touring powerhouse. In 2022, Billboard reported that McCartney’s career touring grosses had surpassed $1 billion, per Billboard Boxscore figures; at the time, he was one of just 11 artists to ever hit that figure.

Both as one-fourth of The Beatles and as a solo artist, McCartney has forged one of the most commercially successful careers in music of all time. His band still holds the record for most Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 hits of all time with a total of 20, and McCartney has also topped the chart nine other times through his independent work and with Wings, which he formed in 1971 after The Beatles broke up.

He’s been similarly successful on the Billboard 20 0 , scoring 19 No. 1s with The Beatles and eight individually or with Wings.

entertainment.title: No ‘Maybe’ About It: Carly Rae Jepsen to Host & Perform at 2027 Juno Awards
entertainment.summary: The pop star’s earworm “Call Me Maybe” won single of the year at the Junos in 2013.
entertainment.body:
Carly Rae Jepsen is set to host the 2027 Juno Awards , which will be held at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, on Sunday, April 4.

Jepsen’s global smash “Call Me Maybe” — which was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for nine weeks in 2012 — won single of the year at the 2013 Juno Awards . Kiss , the album which featured the earworm, won album of the year and pop album of the year. “Call Me Maybe” also got some love at the 2013 Grammy Awards, receiving nominations for song of the year and best pop solo performance.

This will be Jepsen’s first time hosting the Juno Awards. The show has been hosted by many of the biggest Canadian music stars, including Shania Twain (2003), Alanis Morissette (2004), Nelly Furtado (2007 and 2024), Drake (2011), Michael Bublé (2013, 2018 and 2025), Bryan Adams (2017) and Sarah McLachlan (2019).

Angine de Poitrine is also set to perform on the show. The Quebec duo, consisting of brothers Klek and Khn de Poitrine, has had a breakout year, taking home the 2026 Polaris Music Prize, SOCAN Polaris Song Prize, Billboard Canada Power Players 2026 Global Breakthrough Award and 11 Felix award nominations.

Canadian rock band Our Lady Peace , who has received four Juno Awards, will be inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame and take the stage for a live performance.

The Juno Awards have been on the move among major Canadian cities since 1989. This will be the show’s third time in Winnipeg, following the shows in 2005 and 2014.

“We’re thrilled to bring The Juno Awards back to Winnipeg, a city with such a rich musical history and a deep appreciation for Canadian talent,” Allan Reid, president and CEO, Canadian Academy of Recording Arts & Sciences/The Juno Awards, said in a statement.

The 56th Annual Juno Awards, produced by Insight Productions (A Blue Ant Studios Company), will air live across Canada at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on CBC TV, CBC Gem, CBC Radio One, CBC Music, CBC listen, and stream globally on the CBC’s website and on CBC Music’s YouTube channel.

entertainment.title: ‘Survivor 51’ Castoff Brady Booker on That “Toxicity” Comment, Starving Through Challenges and What It Means to Be a “Brodie”
entertainment.summary: The professional wrestler opens up about his blindside elimination, why he believes his personality rubbed some players the wrong way and how hunger pushed him to his limits.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Professional wrestler Brady brought plenty of energy, intensity and a whole lot of “brodies” to Survivor 51 , but his aggressive gameplay ultimately caught up with him at the merge. After a chaotic Tribal Council saw even his closest allies turn against him in a 9-4 vote on the Nov. 4 episode, the normally outspoken Brady left without saying a word. In his exit interview with The Hollywood Reporter below, Brady explains his unusually quiet departure, responds to Jelly’s harsh criticism of his behavior and reveals just how much the lack of food affected him physically and emotionally. Related Stories General News Trump Reflects on Republicans' Midterm Losses, Reacts to J.D. Vance's Own Analysis in '60 Minutes' Interview TV Chris Pratt Tapped for King of Comedy Award at 2026 Kids' Choice Awards

Let’s start with your exit. You’re a pretty outgoing guy, so it was surprising to see you leave without saying a word. What was going through your mind at that moment?

I figured I was going to get some votes, but when I got to about six, I started to “read the room.” When Jeff [Probst, host] reads that last vote, it’s like a flash bang goes off. Everything just went “Eek!” and my soul left my body. When I do something brodie, I do it 110 percent. I’m balls to the wall. And when the competition ends, when that weight falls off you, you almost go back to being a regular person.

I know that’s tough for people to believe. I do always have this energy, but man, it’s a different animal when I’m competing. I’ve done it at a high level with high intensity. I find that chaos fun, which is maybe why I tried to turn the game into a little bit of chaos myself. But me walking out and not saying anything was that quick thought of, “Do I blow up the game?” And that’s not how I would want it to be played. Now it’s my job to be on the jury.

AAs I’m walking up there, you realize the surreal moment of what you’re going through. Only so many people have actually got to go through that. I took it all in — took in Jeff’s beautiful face one last time — and then I took my walk.

Maggie, Kilby and Kristin all seemed to be firmly in your corner, yet all three voted against you. Did you see any signs they might turn on you, or did those votes completely blindside you?

No, because I was worried about Kristin from the jump once Mike blew that all up. She wanted to believe me, but then I guess as it came closer to tribal and people started to hear numbers; she just ended up believing what the numbers were at. Kilby was advocating for me during tribal. But with the drama he had with Eric and him not wanting to write his name down again because I guess that’s the other option, he was looking out for his game. Then Carter and Lewis, both their names were getting thrown out. I guess that wasn’t shown as much, but they were also worried about themselves. So I appreciate them riding or dying for your boy.

The Jets only allowed 30 points over the first two weeks of the season, but they’ve allowed 193 in the last seven games. That includes Sunday’s 35-point performance by the Chiefs and the Jets have only won one of those seven contests to drop to 2-7 on the season.

On Monday, Glenn was asked at a press conference if he would consider handing off the play-calling role to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in the second half of the season.

“Well, I would say this, and listen, we have not played really good defense the last couple of weeks, and I am very aware of that,” Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. “But again, there’s been evidence of us playing really good defense throughout this season and listen, I will never say never to anything, but I do know this: I’m looking at everything and I’m looking of ways of us to improve, and whatever that is for us to get better, you can best believe I’ll make those changes. And I think I’ve done that throughout my career to be able to do that is I’m not afraid to make a change. I’m not saying that is going to be the change, but I’m looking at everything.”

Given the Jets’ record, it’s hard to imagine too many little tweaks that are going to lead to a major change in circumstances for the team. It’s also hard to imagine Glenn doing much to improve his chances of sticking around after a 5-21 start to his tenure, but we’ll see if anything looks different when the Jets face the Bills at home in Week 10.

sports.title: Andy Reid on Harrison Butker: I haven’t made any decisions yet
sports.summary: The Chiefs have a clear and obvious kicking problem.
sports.body:
Harrison Butker officially missed one more field goal on Sunday, sailing a 51-yard attempt wide right.

But everyone also saw him miss from 56 a snap before — a play that didn’t count because of a Jets penalty.

Butker has now missed 17 kicks over the last two seasons, which is a league-high.

Kansas City has Justin Tucker on its practice squad, and he would ostensibly be the next man up. But in his Monday news conference, Reid told reporters that he wasn’t ready to commit to any changes at kicker.

“With Butker, I haven’t made any decisions yet,” Reid said. “I’m going to evaluate everything and go forward from there. Again, I haven’t decided on reps during practice, I haven’t done any of that right now. Just going through it, evaluating. And we’ll go from there.”

Butker has made just 12-of-19 field goals so far this season. He’s also missed an extra point.

We’ll see if Reid has more to say about his kicker situation when the Chiefs start their practice week on Wednesday.

sports.title: Zac Taylor: Bengals are good where we are, expect nothing at the trade deadline
sports.summary: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor says nothing is happening in Cincinnati at the NFL trade deadline.
sports.body:
Asked today what he expects to happen between now and tomorrow at 4 p.m., Taylor said he doesn’t expect anything to happen.

“Nothing. That’s a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we’re good,” Taylor said.

Asked by another reporter whether there are positions he thinks his team still needs help at, Taylor said he likes the roster he has.

The Bengals are 6-2 and in the thick of the AFC playoff race, and Taylor has his team right where he wants to be.

sports.title: Bills-Vikings game carries major significance for both teams
sports.summary: The Bills and Vikings have identical 0-4 records in the Super Bowl.
sports.body:
For Buffalo, which hopes to force the January road to SoFi Stadium through the open-air new venue in Western New York, it’s important to maintain distance between the 6-2 Jaguars and 7-2 Broncos. (The division is looking like the Bills’ to lose, with the Patriots now at 5-4.)

For Minnesota, their status as the last unbeaten team in the NFL could dissolve to being the last team out of the NFC playoff picture.

The NFC North, which now has a 20-3 record outside the division, has the Vikings at 6-1, the Lions at 6-2, the Bears at 6-2, and the Packers at 6-3. (Combined, they’ve lost as many games as the 0-8 Chargers.)

Last week, when the Vikings picked up their first loss of the season, the Lions, Bears, and Packers won. This week, the Lions, Bears, and Packers have won. A loss by the Vikings would conclude a two-week window in which the Vikings are 0-2, and the rest of the division is 6-0.

It gets worse. The 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams each won on Sunday. In the end, five playoff berths will go to the four teams of the NFC North and top three teams of the NFC West.

Two of those teams will be left out. And, frankly, the Vikings seem destined to be one of them.

Even with a 6-2 record, if they lose to the Bills. Because even though the defense is good enough to win a Super Bowl, the offense isn’t good enough to win a playoff game. It could be just bad enough to keep the team from making the playoffs.

It was one thing for the Vikings’ defense to not gripe when the end result of each game was victory. If the second game of a four-week gauntlet doesn’t go Minnesota’s way (the Packers and 49ers are up next), things could get even more awkward in the locker room.

sports.title: Kevin Stefanski on Jessie Bates trade: Falcons aren't punting on the season
sports.summary: The Falcons traded veteran safety Jessie Bates to the Jaguars today, which some might see as a sign that the Falcons don't see themselves as contenders and are looking ahead at 2027.
sports.body:
Stefanski did acknowledge that the Falcons are building for the future, but he also noted that in the NFC South, Atlanta remains very much in contention at 3-6.

“You guys know how I feel about Jessie the person, Jessie the player,” Stefanski told reporters. “But at the same time, this is football, where sometimes you have one foot in the short term, one foot in the long term. There’s things like this that make your team better in the long run. Draft picks are the life blood of an organization. That’s something we believe in.

Stefanski said he wants fans to know that they still are going to compete to win the NFC South.

“Our fans are smart enough to know that in no way, shape or form would we punt on this season. We have three wins, just like the rest of our division. Obviously not where we want to be, we want to play better, but we’re in the thick of this thing and we trust in the guys we have,” Stefanski said.

The Falcons might not be punting on the season, but they are deciding to move on from a player who can help them this season and get draft picks for future seasons. The Falcons still might win the worst division in football, but today’s trade is not the trade pf a team that thinks it’s a Super Bowl contender this year.

sports.title: Greg Olsen accuses media of putting "words in my mouth" about Malik Nabers
sports.summary: After Sunday's win over the Eagles, Giants receiver Malik Nabers had some things to say about things Fox's Greg Olsen had to say about Nabers during the game.
sports.body:
On Monday, Olsen had some things to say about how the New York Post and USA Today characterized the things he said.

Olsen accused those publications of making up quotes and putting “worlds [sic] in my mouth.”

In order to avoid any doubt about what Olsen (and others on the Fox broadcast) said — and didn’t say — about Nabers, we went to the video (and audio).

Early in the fourth quarter of the Giants-Eagles game, after Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a pass behind an open Nabers who was running right to left, the Fox cameras showed Nabers waving an arm in apparent frustration.

Said Fox’s Joe Davis, regarding Nabers: “His body language has been terrible today.”

“You brought up Malik Nabers,” Olsen said, “and you never know exactly what’s being said. It’s easy for us to sit here and interpret body language. When we asked [offensive coordinator] Matt Nagy about him, he said, ‘Listen, he’s very vocal. When he didn’t get the ball to start the year, he let everyone know it.’ He said, ‘Me and Malik have a good understanding right now. What’s perceived as being negative, what’s perceived as being a distraction, I think we both have an understanding of each other that allows it to coexist.’ And just certainly is something to keep an eye on.”

Not long after that, the booth threw to Fox sideline reporter Pam Oliver for more on Nabers.

“Yeah, you guys talk about his body language,” Oliver said. “I can tell you a little more about his mindset. I talked to him. And he told me, ‘I just demand excellence out of everybody around me. Anybody that has a hand in my career. Because you only get one shot. It’s your life, it’s your career.’ It’s fueled by a great sense of urgency in that hard-fought return to the field from that knee injury. Nabers said — told me, ‘I’m not going out there running all these routes not to get the ball.’”

sports.title: Lions agree to acquire S Andre Cisco from Jets
sports.summary: Detroit is bringing in some secondary help.
sports.body:
The Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports.

Cisco has appeared in nine games with four starts this year, recording 23 total tackles with two tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defensed.

A third-round pick in the 2021 draft, Cisco played his first four seasons with the Jaguars.

In 80 career games with 59 starts, he’s tallied eight interceptions, 26 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, and six tackles for loss.

With the trade, Cisco is now in line to potentially play 18 games this season. The Lions had their bye in Week 6 and the Jets are not slated to have theirs until Week 13.

sports.title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
sports.summary: Reid said he had seen Mahomes on Monday and the QB was in "good spirits."
sports.body:
It sounds like he might not miss any further playing time either.

“Patrick, he is really day-to-day right now ,” head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Monday news conference. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of some rehab in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. And we’ll just see where it goes from there.

“But he’s in good spirits today — I have seen him today, so he’s in good spirits today.”

Mahomes suffered the injury late in the first half. In the third quarter, he completed 7-of-10 passes for 81 yards. He was 5-of-6 for 41 yards in the fourth quarter.

Additionally, Reid mentioned Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and Jaylon Moore (ankle) are day-to-day with their respective injuries.

The Chiefs will be on the road to play the Falcons in Week 10. The first injury report of the week will be issued on Wednesday.

sports.title: Report: Saints agree to trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars
sports.summary: The Jaguars weren't done trading when they swung a deal to acquire safety Jessie Bates on Monday morning.
sports.body:
Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that they have also agreed to a trade with the Saints for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Other reports indicate a 2028 sixth-round pick will head back to New Orleans.

Bates is joining the team in a trade with the Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection.

Godchaux appeared in all eight Saints games this season and he made five starts before moving into a reserve role for the last three contests. He had 15 tackles and a tackle for loss in those appearances.

Godchaux was in his second season with the Saints. He previously played for the Patriots and Dolphins. He and Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile overlapped with the Dolphins during the 2020 season.

The Jaguars lost DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending quad injury in Week 8 and Godchaux gives them another experienced option to help fill the void.

UPDATE 1:46 p.m. ET : Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the 2028 sixth-round pick is a conditional one. The Jaguars currently do not have a 2027 sixth-rounder, but will send one to the Saints if they acquire one at some point ahead of the draft.

sports.title: NFL moves Jaguars-Giants game in Week 11 to a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff
sports.summary: The NFL announced a couple of changes to kickoff times for Week 11 of the 2026 season.
sports.body:
The Jaguars and Giants were originally scheduled to start their game at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on November 22, but the game will now get underway at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Steelers’ visit to Philadelphia to face the Eagles was set for that time and it will now take over the 1 p.m. slot.

Both games will still be broadcast by CBS and the Jaguars-Giants contest is now set to be the network’s national game during that window. It’s a sensible change as both teams are leading their divisions while the Eagles, who have a bye in Week 10, will carry a seven-game losing streak into their matchup with the Steelers.

A Raiders-Broncos game in Denver will also start at 4:25 p.m. ET and the Jets-Chargers game in Los Angeles will be the lone 4:05 p.m. ET start that weekend.

sports.title: Tom Brady: "There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today"
sports.summary: The quarterback with a statue outside the stadium returned for the first time to call a game in his capacity as a broadcaster for Fox.
sports.body:
After the Packers blew out the Patriots at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, former Patriots quarterback Tom Brady made an observation about the current Patriots quarterback.

“There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today,” Brady said to Packers safety Evan Williams in a post-game interview.

Replied Williams: “I’m not gonna say that, but he was giving us some gifts, for sure.”

It was funny and light-hearted. And, frankly, not inaccurate.

The “deli meat” insult has recently become a thing. After the Rams’ Week 8 win over the Chargers, Rams safety Quentin Lake said Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was throwing “ deli meat .” Lake later apologized .

More generally, the comments highlight one of the basic realities of Brady calling NFL games while owning a piece of the Raiders. To date, he hasn’t called a Raiders game. One of these days, he likely will.

What if Fernando Mendoza gives out “deli meat”? What if the head coach makes a questionable decision? What if any of the Raiders players do something that would invite scrutiny and/or criticism?

For now, Fox and the NFL can stickhandle the scheduling to keep Brady out of the delicate spot of working a Raiders game. It would become unavoidable only if the Raiders make it to the Super Bowl in a year that Fox will be broadcasting the game.

sports.title: Sam Darnold ruled out for Week 10, Drew Lock in line to start
sports.summary: Sam Darnold will be out for at least another week, but the Seahawks' regular backup quarterback should be able to play in the Week 10 matchup against the Raiders.
sports.body:
Head coach Mike Macdonald said in his weekly interview with Seattle Sports 710’s Brock Huard and Mike Salk that Darnold will miss another game with his quad injury. But the team is planning to start Drew Lock again, even though he was injured during Sunday’s win over the Cardinals.

“Good exam for Drew,” Macdonald said, via Andrew Destin of TheAthletic.com. “He’s dealing with an oblique. And, I think it’s something we can manage .”

Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards with a touchdown in the 17-3 victory over the Cardinals. he also rushed five times for 16 yards.

While Lock has also been dealing with an elbow issue, the Seahawks kept him limited on the report for all three days last week before he had no game status and started against Arizona. The plan could be similar for Lock in Week 10.

Jalen Milroe is Seattle’s third quarterback, though he has not appeared in a game so far in 2026.

sports.title: John Harbaugh says it "looks like" QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) will be able to play on Thursday
sports.summary: The NFL has fully embraced a full slate of Thursday night games, justifying the health-and-safety realities by pointing to in-game injury rates when a team has a full week to rest and when it has a four-day turnaround.
sports.body:
That selective statistical focus overlooks the basic reality that some players injured on one Sunday would be ready by the next Sunday, but won’t be ready by Thursday.

For Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the three extra days to recover from the hip pointer he suffered on Sunday would be useful. As it stands, the clock is ticking toward Thursday night’s game against the Commanders.

Coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Monday that McCarthy is “doing well,” and that it “ does look like he’s going to play ” on Thursday night.

Even if he’s not playing, there’s strategic value in keeping the Commanders in the dark about whether it will be McCarthy or Jameis Winston. Either way, it would be wise for Washington to be ready for both guys, since McCarthy could aggravate the injury or suffer a new one.

That’s the reality of rolling with McCarthy. His fearlessness means he’ll take hits. The more hits he takes, the more likely it is that he’ll be hurt.

Winston did well during the brief time McCarthy went to the locker room, presumably for a quick visit with Dr. Needle. Winston completed six passes for 71 yards and a touchdown — half of the total passes McCarthy completed in the rest of the game.

In the end, the Giants got another win. They’re 5-2-1. And they’re taking control of the NFC East, especially with the Eagles at 2-7, the Commanders at 2-5-1, and the Cowboys at 4-5.

McCarthy has a higher floor than Winston. Winston, when things are clicking, could have a higher ceiling. And he seems to be better when he enters a game cold, giving the Giants the best of both worlds as they try to turn a season that seemed lost seven weeks ago tonight into something special.

sports.title: College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in $1.7 billion ESPN deal
sports.summary: The College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams in 2027 under a $1.7 billion deal with ESPN, eliminating Power 4 conference championship games.

sports.title: Giants expect Cam Skattebo to play on Thursday night
sports.summary: The Giants played without running back Cam Skattebo in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles, but they do not expect his absence from the lineup to linger.
sports.body:
Head coach John Harbaugh said at a Monday press conference that the expectation is that Skattebo will be “full go” for Thursday night’s game against the Commanders.

Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury late in the Giants’ Week 7 win over the Texans and missed practice for two days coming out of the bye week. He returned on Friday and Harbaugh said he was close to being ready for the Eagles, but that the team had the quick turnaround in mind when making a plan for managing his health.

Devin Singletary was the lead back for the Giants against the Eagles and he ran 21 times for 31 yards. Gregory Desrosiers had 20 yards on three carries.

sports.title: Maxx Crosby on trade deadline: I expect to play for the Raiders
sports.summary: Earlier this year, Maxx Crosby was supposed to be traded from the Raiders to the Ravens.
sports.body:
As is well known, that deal came off the table when Baltimore had concerns about Crosby’s physical.

With the trade deadline approaching, Las Vegas could, in theory, look to trade Crosby again. But the star edge rusher said after Sunday’s loss to the 49ers that he isn’t looking to leave.

“ I play for the Raiders ,” Crosby said, via Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . “I expect to play for the Raiders. That’s all that matters. I love this team, and I plan on being here for a very long time.”

While Crosby pushed for a trade in the offseason, he’s now on board with the direction of the franchise.

“We’re right in the mix,” Crosby said. “We’re 4-5. We had a tough loss today, but when we’re at our best, we can beat anyone. We know it’s going to be a tough challenge. We’ve got a lot of football left and we have to take them one at a time. We’re right in the middle of it. This is the best time of the year. This is what you’ve worked so hard for.”

Crosby added he’s not looking for there to be any ambiguity about his desire to remain with the franchise that drafted him.

“There’s always narratives and always people that supposedly have all this inside information,” Crosby said. “I speak very clearly because everyone has an opinion, but nobody really (knows anything). Everyone that has these random things that come out of nowhere is just trying to get some attention and clickbait. So it’s just part of the game. It comes with being a player of my stature and comes with the nature of the business.

“I don’t pay attention to it. I just hear through the grapevine what’s going on. [I just try to] be present. Focus on what I need to do. Be a great leader, great player and win games in the silver and black. That’s what I plan on doing for a long time.”

sports.title: Report: Browns to start Deshaun Watson against Texans
sports.summary: Watson did not play Sunday, but the team is expected to turn back to him in Week 10.
sports.body:
Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that the plan is for Deshaun Watson to return to the starting lineup against the Texans. Watson cleared concussion protocol on Saturday, but was inactive after missing two practices during the week.

Shedeur Sanders got the start and went 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Monken said after the game that he was proud of Sanders’s performance after spending the first two months of the season on the bench, but declined to answer whether it was enough for him to consider making a lasting change.

Monken hasn’t confirmed the team’s plan, but it appears the team will return to the status quo as they try to keep pace in the AFC playoff race.

sports.title: Patriots don't expect Ben Brown to play in Week 10, waiting for Rhamondre Stevenson MRI results
sports.summary: The Patriots expect to be without guard Ben Brown when they face the Lions in Germany in Week 10.
sports.body:
Brown injured his knee during Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Packers and head coach Mike Vrabel said at a Monday press conference that he doesn’t think Brown will be in the lineup for that game. Brown started at left guard and he was replaced by Walter Rouse.

The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries at guard. Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker are both on injured reserve, which has pushed Matt Pryor into the starting lineup.

Vrabel also said that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is getting an MRI on his knee and that the team does not have an update on his condition at this point. TreVeyon Henderson is out as he looks for answers to a neurological condition, which leaves Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as the team’s healthy backs.

Wide receiver A.J. Brown missed his second straight game with a knee injury and Vrabel said the team is unsure if he’ll be able to play in Munich.

sports.title: Jaguars announce Jessie Bates trade
sports.summary: The Jaguars announced their trade for safety Jessie Bates on Monday.
sports.body:
Bates is headed to Jacksonville to strengthen a position that’s been hit by injuries this season. Eric Murray will miss the rest of the year with an elbow injury and Antonio Johnson missed Week 8 with an ankle injury before returning for last Thursday’s win over the Ravens.

“Jessie has been a proven playmaker on the defensive side of the ball for the last 8+ seasons,” Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone said in a statement. “His skillset complements our style of play and the person he is aligns with our culture. We look forward to integrating Jessie into our team as we prepare for the back half of the season.”

The Jaguars are sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to the Falcons. The Falcons also agreed to pay the bulk of Bates’s salary for the rest of this season. Bates is set to be a free agent in March.

Bates was a second-team All-Pro for the third time in his career last season. He has one interception this season and had 14 in his three-plus years with the Falcons.

sports.title: Ben Johnson benched Zavion Thomas after 15-yard penalty
sports.summary: Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas hasn't had a lot of production so far this season, and he may have even less after head coach Ben Johnson benched him during Sunday night's win over the Buccaneers.
sports.body:
In the second quarter, with the Bears at the Buccaneers’ 6-yard line, Thomas got into a shoving match with Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish and was flagged for unnecessary roughness, moving the Bears back to the 21-yard line. On the next play, Caleb Williams threw an interception, on a play that wouldn’t have been called if the Bears were still at the 6, ending a promising drive. Johnson was not happy.

Asked after the game whether he said anything to Thomas, Johnson answered, “Yeah, I don’t know that he played on offense after that.”

Johnson didn’t need to say any more than to tell Thomas he wouldn’t be going back into the game on offense. (Thomas did keep playing on kickoff returns.) Thomas is a speedy receiver and a talented playmaker, but Johnson wants him to know that he’s not good enough to get away with committing 15-yard penalties.

sports.title: ESPN, CFP strike deal to expand college playoff to 24 teams
sports.summary: For any business, there are two ways to maximize profit.
sports.body:
As to the former, the NCAA (working in cahoots with ESPN, among others) hope to use the wolf-in-sheep’s-clothing of the Protect College Sports Act to reduce the booster’s billions that are currently being diverted to NIL collectives. (The PCSA appears to be DOA , which is good news for the players.)

As to the latter, the NCAA and ESPN have agreed to double the size of the playoff field to 24 as of 2027. Under a five-year, $1.7 billion deal, there will be more postseason games that matter — and fewer postseason Pop Tart/mayonnaise bowl games that don’t.

Along the way, four postseason games that matter plenty are going the way of the dodo bird. The conference championship games for the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, and Big 12 will end.

Under the new schedule, “Week Zero” becomes Week 1. And the regular-season ends on Thanksgiving weekend.

The top eight teams in the CFP rankings will secure byes. The first round (with No. 9 through No. 24 playing games against each other) will cut the field to 16.

In round two, there will be blowouts. The No. 1 seed will play the winner of the game between No. 16 and No. 17. The No. 2 seed will play the winner of No. 15 vs. No. 18.

There also will be new pressure on players who are draft-ready to keep playing, in pursuit of a potential championship. As illusory as that goal may be.

And the players, by all appearances, once again had no seat at the table. More games? No problem.

sports.title: Robert Saleh: Calvin Ridley's airport incident was "a very minor miscommunication"
sports.summary: News emerged on Sunday night that Titans receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident over the weekend at Nashville International Airport.
sports.body:
Few details about the incident have been made public, which continues to be the case after head coach Robert Saleh’s news conference on Monday.

“With regards to Calvin, we’re aware of everything that’s happening,” Saleh said. “From my understanding, it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport . Unfortunately, law enforcement has it, and that’s about as far as I can go with commenting.”

It’s been a rough 2026 for the Titans so far, as they’ve won just one game and have dealt with multiple off-the-field incidents.

“Ultimately, when you’re losing, everything is kind of exacerbated,” Saleh said. “But all 32 buildings deal with things throughout the season. It’s unfortunate with what happened, but I’m sure we’ll move on with business as normal.”

Coming off their Week 9 bye, the Titans will host the division-rival Jaguars in Week 10.

sports.title: Jaguars agree to trade for Falcons S Jessie Bates
sports.summary: Jacksonville makes a move to improve their defense ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
sports.body:
According to multiple reports, they have agreed to trade for Falcons safety Jessie Bates. The Jaguars will send a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons in exchange for Bates.

Bates was named a second-team All-Pro for the third time in his career last season and he has 60 tackles, an interception, three forced fumbles and a fumble return for a touchdown in nine games this season. He is in the final year of the four-year contract he signed with Atlanta in 2023 and reports indicate the Falcons will pick up most of his remaining salary to facilitate the trade.

The Jaguars, who improved to 6-2 with Thursday’s win over the Ravens, lost safety Eric Murray to a season-ending elbow injury recently and Antonio Johnson has also dealt with injuries, so Bates gives them the stability and high-end play they need at the position.
