sports.body: Over the last several weeks, we have seen the classic unraveling of a Jets season. The faces change, but the results always seem to stay the same. Entering Week 7, the Jets faced a two game homestand against beatable opponents. Victories against both the Dolphins and the Raiders would get the team to .500 through eight games and give this team real momentum heading into a tough stretch facing the Chiefs and Bills back-to-back. Of course, the Jets handed the previously winless Dolphins their first victory and then lost to the Raiders, dropping their record to 2-6. Not even at the halfway point, the season was over. It is normal for the competitive portion of the season to end early for Jets fans. It feels like an annual tradition in November to be discussing NFL Draft position above all else. The only thing the Jets still had going for them is it felt like the team was still united. Players were fighting for each other. Things changed in the Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets looked like an imploding team. Fans could see it in obvious ways like Minkah Fitzpatrick making a couple of business decisions when he had opportunities to make plays. Armand Membou threw his helmet in frustration in an emotional outburst after allow a second half sack. Geno Smith was demonstrative in his frustration frequently as the game slipped away. These are symptoms of a season that is slipping away and a team that is in a spiral. Through each offseason NFL fans of all 32 teams convince themselves that their team has made all of the right moves, and their roster is improved. That’s part of being a fan. At this time of year, Jets fans frequently are forced to confront the reality that the team made bad moves in the previous offseason, and that has a lot to do with the team’s struggles. The Jets might not have gotten everything wrong in the 2026 offseason. David Bailey increasingly looks like a budding star. If the two pass catchers the Jets took in the first round of the NFL Draft after Bailey aren’t dominating, they at least look promising. Still, at this point I think the obvious is staring Jets fans in the face. This remains a bottom tier roster, and many of the offseason moves that provided hope in March were poor decisions in hindsight, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. sports.summary: The Buccaneers were flagged for five false starts on Sunday night, and quarterback Baker Mayfield said at least one of them was caused by an illegal tactic by the Bears.
sports.body:
Mayfield said left tackle Tristan Wirfs jumped when Bears players yelled Mayfield’s cadence, something that is a penalty when the officials notice it but is hard for the officials to know. Mayfield said he’s not sure what else the Bucs could have done.

“I don’t know,” Mayfield said. “The last one, I know they were barking out the cadence, which you can’t do that. It’s tough for the refs to call that because they’re not right there at the line of scrimmage. They called that on Tristan, but you can’t do that.”

That last false start Mayfield referenced came during a brutal stretch for the Bucs’ offense: Immediately after that false start, Mayfield was hit while throwing an incomplete pass, and on the next three plays Mayfield was sacked, although one of the sacks was wiped out by a penalty. The Bucs’ offensive line looked out of sorts, and Mayfield thinks the Bears’ cheating was a contributing factor.

sports.title: Malik Nabers: Fox tried to "create a narrative" about me being a bad teammate
sports.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took to social media on Sunday night to express his displeasure with how he was portrayed during the Fox broadcast of his team's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
sports.body:
In a post to his Instagram story that was later taken down, Nabers took particular issue with Greg Olsen’s characterization of him. After quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a pass behind Nabers in the fourth quarter, Fox showed Nabers gesturing with his hands and Olsen said he was letting the quarterback know to put the ball in front of him. Play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said Nabers’s “body language has been terrible” throughout the game with Olsen agreeing that it wasn’t good.

The broadcast also showed Nabers slamming his helmet on the sideline at one point and sideline reporter Pam Oliver discussed Nabers’s desire to have the ball come his way. Olsen went on to say that there is “a fine line” between receivers demanding the ball and being overly worried about your own touches that it detracts from the success of others. Nabers responded to what he believes was an implication that he’s a bad teammate.

“Y’all be trying [to] create a narrative on me soo bad, it’s actually crazy!! If you [don’t] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE! But [Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I’ve been on, there’s NOBODY I’ve played with has said dat bout me is crazy! My face the same way if I’m havin a good game, bad, winning or losing,” Nabers wrote. “If it’s a problem. 1. Keep the camera off of me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple.”

Nabers finished the game with five catches for 43 yards, which snapped a four-game streak with at least 111 receiving yards. He said in his postgame media session that he was frustrated with how the offense played at points in Philadelphia, but his frustration with Olsen and Davis might have been even greater.

sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. sports.title: Drew Lock and the Seahawks earn an easy win over the Cardinals
sports.summary: As he has been all season, Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock was a steady hand running the offense.
sports.body:
Lock, playing once again for an injured Sam Darnold, was steady and efficient as the Seahawks controlled the game and beat the Cardinals 17-3.

Is Lock a better quarterback than Darnold? Probably not, but Lock might be better for what the Seahawks need right now, which is a quarterback who can play mistake-free football and let the defense win the game. Darnold has thrown nine interceptions this season, while Lock has thrown none.

Today Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and one touchdown. Not spectacular numbers, but the key numbers were zeroes: Zero interceptions, zero fumbles, zero sacks. Darnold has far more negative plays than Lock does this season, and that’s one of the reasons the Seahawks are 3-0 in the three games that have been primarily quarterbacked by Lock, and 2-4 in the six games that have primarily been quarterbacked by Darnold.

At 5-4, the Seahawks aren’t the team they hoped to be heading into this season, but they’re very much in contention. And they might just have a better chance of making the playoffs and getting an opportunity to defend their title if Lock keeps playing.

sports.summary: The 49ers offense has been tough to stop all year and that has remained the case in Sunday’s game against the Raiders.
sports.body:
San Francisco turned long drives into touchdowns on each of the club’s first three possessions to take a 21-10 lead into halftime.

The 49ers got on the board with a 1-yard touchdown run by Christian McCaffrey. It’s his seventh consecutive game with a touchdown run, which is now the longest streak in a season in team history.

Quarterback Brock Purdy had a 1-yard touchdown run to put the 49ers up 14-0, finishing off a 13-play, 89-yard drive.

McCaffrey then had a 12-yard receiving touchdown, giving San Francisco three scoring drives of at least 12 plays to begin the game.

The only time the 49ers didn’t get going was in a potential two-minute drive, with the offense going backward on a sack and an illegal shift.

Purdy was 8-of-12 for 123 yards with a touchdown plus six carries for 40 yards with a TD in the first half.

On the other side, Kirk Cousins had the Raiders’ touchdown early in the second quarter with a 2-yard QB sneak. Ironically, that made him the team’s rushing touchdown leader this season with two.

sports.title: Saints hang on to defeat Browns in overtime, 23-22
sports.summary: The Browns and Saints were tied at 6-6 midway through the fourth quarter.
sports.body:
But the game then became a barn burner in the final period and overtime, with a failed Cleveland two-point conversion allowing the Saints to escape with a narrow 23-22 victory.

New Orleans had taken a 9-6 lead with Charlie Smyth’s 48-yard field goal with 5:38 left in the contest. But the Browns immediately responded with a 64-yard touchdown catch by rookie KC Concepcion, who burned the defense off the line.

The Browns, however, couldn’t hold the late lead. The team’s four-minute offense couldn’t convert enough first downs, leaving the Saints with time to get down the field. They were able to get in the end zone with Audric Estime’s 2-yard touchdown with 58 seconds on the clock, going ahead 16-13.

But Shedeur Sanders — playing after Deshaun Watson spent most of the week in concussion protocol — connected with Jerry Jeudy for a key 30-yard gain. The outstanding throw and catch set up Andre Szmyt for a game-tying 51-yard field goal to send the contest into overtime.

Juwan Johnson capped New Orleans’ OT possession with a 15-yard touchdown reception.

But Harold Fannin’s terrific catch-and-run put the Browns in position to tie it or win it with a 39-yard touchdown. Browns head coach Todd Monken elected to go for the win instead of settling for — at best — a potential tie. But Sanders’ throw to Denzel Boston was incomplete. Even if it had been caught, the Browns were flagged for holding.

Sanders finished the contest 19-of-31 for 297 yards with a pair of touchdowns.

On the other side, Tyler Shough was 21-of-35 for 265 yards with a TD.

The Bills beat the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 last Sunday, but Baltimore lost both quarterbacks in the first half, and I’m careful about using that game as a measuring stick for this one. Minnesota is a different kind of test. Brian Flores is the main reason. His defense leads the NFL in scoring (13.3 points per game) and blitzes on roughly 70 percent of dropbacks. Carolina is next at 42.6 percent (the Bills themselves blitzed on 64.5 percent of dropbacks last Sunday, second only to Minnesota in Week 8, per Next Gen Stats). Josh Allen completes 65.7 percent of his passes against five or more rushers at 8.4 yards per attempt, so, on paper it’s a great matchup but the reality is that nobody is better than Flores sending 5 or more after opposing QBs. Buffalo has the league’s best offense (33.3 points per game) and the best EPA per play (0.175), and Minnesota has the best defensive mark (-0.189). The Vikings’ offense is their problem on the other side. It ranks 30th in EPA per play (-0.099), Carson Wentz starts with Kyler Murray out with a hamstring injury, and Justin Jefferson has 335 yards heading into Week 9, a lower pace than his career-low 2025, per Pro Football Talk. I think the game comes down to whether Buffalo’s offense can stay on schedule against the blitz while the defense tries to not give Wentz and Jefferson easy completions. With all of this in mind, here are the Bills who need to keep rolling and those who must step up Monday night. sports.body: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Garrett Wilson Tim Patrick Blake Freeland Trevin Wallace Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Kohl Levao Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

sports.body: Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith had an expensive day in Orchard Park, NY last weekend. Smith received a heavy dose of fines for his on-field efforts against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. He was fined a total of $35,822 for two infractions, one against quarterback Josh Allen, and a second against wide receiver DJ Moore. The NFL handed Smith a fine of $17,911 for a facemask grab and tug he implemented on quarterback Josh Allen during a successful touchdown sneak, per Tom Pelissero. During the play, Smith was observed grabbing Allen’s facemask while trying to pull him back, then pulling and twisting the helmet aggressively until it ended up completely backwards — and with Allen’s head and neck turning almost a complete 180 degrees. Smith wasn’t penalized following the play.
